title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree Turning To The Quran And Referring To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: He believed the main purpose of life is faith.

questions.question: After speaking to his heart, what book did the traveller decide to examine?
questions.answer: He decided to examine the Qur'an.

questions.question: Before studying what the Qur'an says, what did he think needed to be proven first?
questions.answer: He thought it first had to be shown that the Qur'an comes from the Creator.

questions.question: Why did the traveller look first at the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because he was living in the present age and saw it as a guide that explains the Qur'an.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur described in relation to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It is described as containing bright truths taken from the Qur'an and strong explanations of its meanings.

questions.question: What does the passage say about people trying to defeat the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It says no one can overcome it, even in a stubborn age of unbelief.

questions.question: What does the passage say this strength of the Risale-i Nur shows about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur'an is its true source and authority, and that it is from heaven, not made by people.

questions.question: Which two parts of the Risale-i Nur are said to show many ways the Qur'an is miraculous?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: How many aspects of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature are said to be shown there?
questions.answer: Forty aspects.

questions.question: What reaction does the passage say a fair person would have after seeing that proof?
questions.answer: The person would admire it and praise it instead of criticizing it.

questions.question: Why did the traveller not explain all the proofs in detail here?
questions.answer: Because he left the full proof to the Risale-i Nur and only wanted to mention a few brief points about the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: Who did the traveller speak to at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He spoke to his own heart.

questions.question: How is the traveller described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as someone who does not tire and is never satisfied with shallow searching.

questions.question: What did he say about the Qur'an’s place among books?
questions.answer: He said it is the most well-known, shining, and wise book in the world.

questions.question: What kind of challenge does the Qur'an give in every age?
questions.answer: It challenges those who refuse to accept it.

questions.question: What was the traveller searching for before reading the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: He was searching for proof that it truly comes from Allah.

questions.question: In the present age, what work did he use first in his search?
questions.answer: He used the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: What does the passage say the many sections of the Risale-i Nur are made up of?
questions.answer: They are made up of shining points from the Qur'an and careful explanations of its teachings.

questions.question: What is the Risale-i Nur trying to spread?
questions.answer: It is trying to spread the truths of the Qur'an everywhere.

questions.question: What does the failure of others to defeat the Risale-i Nur suggest about its source?
questions.answer: It suggests that its source is the Qur'an and that the Qur'an is divine speech.

questions.question: What is special about the proof found in the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter?
questions.answer: It explains the Qur'an’s miraculous nature in a very strong and convincing way.

questions.question: What did the traveller say life is really about?
questions.answer: He said life is really about faith.

questions.question: Why did he want to examine the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Because it is said to be the speech of the One he was seeking.

questions.question: What careful step did he want to take before looking at the Qur'an’s teachings?
questions.answer: He wanted first to make sure it truly came from the Creator.

questions.question: Since he lived in modern times, where did he begin his investigation?
questions.answer: He began with the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur draws from?
questions.answer: It draws from the Qur'an.

questions.question: In what kind of age is the Risale-i Nur described as working hard?
questions.answer: It is working hard in an age marked by stubborn denial and atheism.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the fact that no one can defeat the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that the Qur'an is its master and source, and that the Qur'an is not human speech.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter help prove?
questions.answer: They help prove that the Qur'an has many miraculous qualities.

questions.question: How many miraculous qualities are mentioned in that proof?
questions.answer: Forty are mentioned.

questions.question: What happens to someone who truly sees that proof, according to the passage?
questions.answer: That person stops objecting and begins to admire the evidence.

questions.question: What did the traveller choose to do after that?
questions.answer: He chose to leave the detailed proof to the Risale-i Nur and mention only a few signs of the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: What did he call the Qur'an besides a book?
questions.answer: He treated it as the speech of the Being he was searching for.

questions.question: What had to be settled first before studying the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: It had to be settled that the Qur'an is from the Creator.

questions.question: What was the traveller’s first source in this age for understanding the Qur'an?
questions.answer: His first source was the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Risale-i Nur to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It presents it as a work that reflects the Qur'an’s light and explains its meanings.

questions.question: What does the passage say about attempts to overcome the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It says those attempts fail.

questions.question: What bigger truth is supported by that failure?
questions.answer: It supports the truth that the Qur'an is its heavenly source.

questions.question: Which writings are named as giving one strong proof for the Qur'an’s miraculous nature?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the conclusion of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: What do these writings make a reader feel instead of fault-finding?
questions.answer: They make the reader feel admiration and appreciation.

questions.question: Why does the traveller give only a short mention of the Qur'an’s greatness here?
questions.answer: Because the fuller demonstration is already given elsewhere, so he only points to a few key signs.

questions.question: What did the traveller know about the goal of life?
questions.answer: He knew that the goal and core of life is faith.

questions.question: What action did he take after talking to his heart?
questions.answer: He began to look into the Qur'an.

questions.question: What made the Qur'an important enough for him to examine?
questions.answer: It was believed to be the word of the One he was seeking and to be the greatest and wisest book.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur'an does to those who reject it?
questions.answer: It confronts them with a challenge in every age.

questions.question: Before asking what the Qur'an teaches, what question did the traveller want answered?
questions.answer: He wanted to know whether it truly came from Allah.

questions.question: What did he study first because he lived in the current time?
questions.answer: He studied the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: How are the parts of the Risale-i Nur described?
questions.answer: They are described as shining lessons taken from the Qur'an and sound explanations of it.

questions.question: What does its success in a difficult age show?
questions.answer: It shows that its power comes from the Qur'an and that the Qur'an is divine speech.

questions.question: What two sections are singled out as especially proving the Qur'an’s extraordinary nature?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: How complete is the proof found there, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is strong enough to show forty different sides of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What method does the traveller use at the end of the passage section?
questions.answer: He points to detailed proof elsewhere and then gives only a short introduction to a few signs of greatness.

questions.question: What important truth about life had the traveller already understood?
questions.answer: He had understood that faith is the true aim and essence of life.

questions.question: To whom did the traveller direct his words before starting his search?
questions.answer: He directed his words to his own heart.

questions.question: What was he hoping to learn by examining the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He was hoping to learn what it says and whether it is truly from the Creator.

questions.question: How is the Qur'an presented in the passage compared with other books?
questions.answer: It is presented as the most famous, radiant, and wise book.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an’s challenge unusual?
questions.answer: It continues across every age, not just one time.

questions.question: Why did the traveller begin with the Risale-i Nur instead of somewhere else?
questions.answer: Because he lived in this age and saw it as a present-day explanation of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the source of the Risale-i Nur’s strength?
questions.answer: Its strength comes from the Qur'an, which is described as heavenly speech.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying no one can defeat the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It implies that the truths it carries are powerful and firmly based on revelation.

questions.question: What is said about the proof in the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter?
questions.answer: It clearly shows many ways the Qur'an is miraculous.

questions.question: What number is given for those ways?
questions.answer: The number given is forty.

questions.question: After noticing these proofs, what did the traveller decide to do next?
questions.answer: He decided to leave the full explanation to the Risale-i Nur and mention only a few brief signs of the Qur'an’s greatness.
